title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Artificial intelligence continues to shift with Anthropic surpassing OpenAI in business customer acquisition, targeting small businesses and driving platform competition. Simultaneously, Notion is integrating AI agents into its workspace platform, expanding into agentic productivity software. A major ransomware attack against Foxconn, impacting Apple, Google, and Nvidia, highlights critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities within interconnected supply chains.

The financial sector is witnessing the rise of perpetual decentralized exchanges (DEXs) like Decibel, attracting institutional interest and potentially reshaping global financial product structures.

Globally, President Trump’s visit to China focuses on trade, Iran, and Taiwan, a pivotal moment for US-China relations. The ongoing conflict in Eastern Europe, marked by Russian strikes on Kyiv, persists with devastating humanitarian consequences. Escalating tensions following Israeli strikes in Lebanon have resulted in casualties, and Cuba faces a severe energy crisis due to a US-led oil blockade. These events contribute to a period of heightened geopolitical and economic instability worldwide.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street opened defensively on Thursday, May 14, 2026, following hotter-than-expected US producer inflation data, with the S&P 500 rising 0.58% and the Nasdaq 100 increasing 1.04%. The 10-Year Treasury Yield decreased to 4.444%, while the US Dollar Index rose and crude oil declined. Overnight, Asian markets experienced mixed performance; Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 fell 0.98%, while Greater China indices saw declines due to trade policy uncertainty. European markets also traded cautiously, influenced by stronger-than-expected UK GDP figures.

US equity futures are showing a modest upward bias, with S&P 500 futures up 0.33% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.29%. Investors are focused on several key catalysts, including the ongoing impact of the PPI data, the Trump-Xi summit, and European economic data, particularly UK GDP and Canadian home sales. The market appears poised for a range-bound session, awaiting significant developments from these data releases.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The US market concluded Wednesday, May 13, 2026, with a nuanced performance driven by growth sector strength despite inflation concerns. The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to 7444.3, while the Nasdaq 100 jumped 1.04% to 29366.943, reflecting continued tech appetite. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.14% to 49693.2. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a retail-driven rally rather than broad institutional buying.

The “Fear Gauge” (VIX) remained subdued at 17.99, indicating controlled rotation and sector-specific gains. A notable divergence emerged, with Technology (XLK) surging 0.94% and Utilities (XLU) falling 1.15%, signaling investor preference for growth over safety. This rotation highlighted a willingness to take on risk for potential upside.

Inflation data played a key role, with a “hot” April PPI report triggering a slight decrease in the 10-Year Treasury Yield to 4.463%, despite market concerns. The US Dollar Index rose 0.20% to 98.38, reacting to the PPI data. Crude Oil prices fell 0.92% to $101.24, influenced by unexpectedly low inventory levels.

Within the Magnificent Seven, Nvidia led the gains, up 2.29%, while Microsoft edged down 0.63%. Alphabet, Meta, and Tesla also saw significant increases, reflecting continued investor confidence in the long-term growth potential of these tech giants. The market’s focus remains on digesting inflation data and anticipating the Federal Reserve’s response.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary: U-S President Donald Trump’s visit to Beijing highlighted ongoing tensions between the world’s largest economies, primarily concerning trade, technology, and regional security. Simultaneously, Iranian military seized a “floating armoury” ship in the Gulf of Oman, escalating regional conflict. In Ukraine, rescuers continued operations following Russian drone and missile strikes, resulting in at least sixteen fatalities. Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned due to criticism over drone incursions, raising border security concerns. The C-I-A chief visited Cuba amid a deepening energy crisis and U-S aid offers. Finally, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon resulted in twenty-two fatalities, including eight children, further escalating violence. These events underscore a complex geopolitical landscape with significant economic and security implications.
